title: SPA/956/2017 of Director Primary Education Nannorkhera Tapowan Uttarakhand AND OTHERS Vs Mahendra Singh Rana

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 956 of 2017
Director Primary Education & others .....Appellants

Versus
Sh. Mahendra Singh Rana .......Respondent
Mr. Vikas Pandey, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand/appellants.
Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocate for the respondent.
Dated: February 16, 2018
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Hon. K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)

1. Appellants are the respondents in the writ petition. The writ
petitioner applied pursuant to the advertisement dated 02.02.2014 for the
post of Assistant Teacher. The writ petitioner was selected and an order
for appointment was issued on 02.10.2014. The writ petitioner joined as
Assistant Teacher on 15.10.2014. On 8.4.2015, the petitioner tendered
his resignation, according to learned counsel for the writ petitioner, on
family grounds. The appointing authority of the petitioner is the Deputy
Education Officer. Thereafter, an advertisement was issued on 17.2.2016
again calling for application from persons for appointment to the post of
Assistant Teacher. The writ petitioner also applied for the same and he
was selected. Thereafter on the basis that petitioner was re-applicant
meaning that while he had already secured appointment, though he
tendered his resignation, his resignation was accepted subject to some
condition, which was not fulfiled by the petitioner, the service of the
petitioner was terminated, which led to the writ petition. Writ petition
was allowed by learned Single Judge. Feeling aggrieved, State
Government has preferred this appeal.

-2-
2. We heard Mr. Vikas Pandey, Brief Holder for the
State/appellant and Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocate for the respondent/writ
petitioner.
3. Supplementary affidavit has been filed today on behalf of
the writ petitioner. Mr. Vikas Pandey, Brief Holder for the
State/appellant seeks time to file objection to the supplementary affidavit
but we are of the view that documents accompanied with the
supplementary affidavit which include Treasury challan, end therefore,
we see no reason to give any time to file objection.
4. Upto the date 8.4.2015, there is no dispute. On the strength
of the Supplementary affidavit and documents accompanying the same,
it is pointed out that on the basis of resignation tendered on 8.4.2015 by
the writ petitioner, the Deputy Education Officer on 18.6.2015 accepted
the resignation of the petitioner, which was subject to the condition that
salary for the period April, 2015 must be deposited by the petitioner. It is
here the bone of contention arises between the parties. On the one hand,
it is submitted that amount of salary for the period of April,2015 was not
deposited on the other hand, it is contended by the learned counsel for
the petitioner that it was deposited by way of treasury challan copy
whereof is annexed as Annexure no. SCA 1 to the Supplementary
affidavit. This annexure tends to show that in fact salary for the period
April, 2015 amounting Rs. 30,625/- was deposited by the petitioner on
12.5.2015. If this document is accepted, then the case of the appellants
that the condition in the order accepting the resignation was not
complied, cannot be accepted.
5. The second advertisement against which petitioner applied
again for the post of Assistant Teacher in Government primary schools
was published only on 7.2.2016.
6. No doubt, it is pointed out by learned counsel for the
petitioner that what happened was salary for the month of May, 2015
also came to be credited in the account of the petitioner. That was
deposited by the petitioner in treasury on 6.4.2016. But that may not
have any effect as far as order accepting the resignation or question
relating to the compliance of the said order is concerned. As the order of

-3-
acceptance only contemplated the deposit of salary for the period of
April, 2015 which was duly complied with in May, 2015 itself and
therefore, the employee and employeer relationship stood severed in
terms of order accepting the resignation dated 8.6.2015.
7. In this case, there can be no dispute that the petitioner
secured employment under the advertisement dated 2.2.2014. It can also
be not disputed that petitioner tendered his resignation on 8.4.2015.
Furthermore, there is the order accepting the resignation on 18.6.2015,
but there was condition attached to the acceptance of the resignation
namely salary for the month of April, 2015 must be deposited by the
petitioner. Documents produced with Supplementary affidavit would
show that the petitioner had deposited a sum of Rs. 30,625 as salary for
the period April, 2015. If that is so the order accepting the resignation
subject to the condition will come into play and the resignation stood
accepted and he ceased to be an employee. If that is so, when petitioner
applied pursuant to the advertisement dated 17.2.2016 he was no longer
employee of State Government and there was no basis for terminating
the services of the petitioner.
8. The fact that the writ petitioner received the salary for the
month of May, 2016 cannot be held against the petitioner for dealing
with petitioner as re-applicant. It is true that there is delay on the part of
the petitioner in depositing the amount, as the amount representing the
salary for the month of May, 2015 was deposited by him in Treasury on
6.4.2016. However, we feel that petitioner must pay interest at the rate of
6% on the said sum, which was credited in his account towards the salary
of May, 2015 from 1st June, 2015 till 6.4.2016 within a period of two
months from today.
9. Subject to the above appeal will stand dismissed. No order
as to costs.
 (Alok Singh, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 16.02.2018
Pankaj
